skill.name: writing-plans
skill.description: Creates detailed, test-driven implementation plans from specifications or requirements before coding begins.
skill.summary: Turn requirements into precise implementation tasks with files, tests, commands, and checkpoints.
skill.author: davila7

content.value_statement: Complex requirements often produce vague tasks and missed tests. This skill creates precise implementation plans with file paths, test steps, commands, and checkpoints.
actual_capabilities: Converts specifications into small, ordered implementation tasks.
Identifies files to create, modify, and test for each task.
Adds test-first steps with expected failure and success outcomes.
Includes exact commands and expected results in generated plans.
Provides execution handoff options after the plan is saved.
limitations: Requires a clear specification or requirements before planning.
Does not implement the plan or run its commands.
Depends on repository context for accurate paths and architecture.
References optional companion skills that may not be installed.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Feature
use_cases.description: Transform approved product requirements into testable engineering tasks with explicit files and commands.

use_cases.title: Prepare Team Handoffs
use_cases.description: Create a self-contained plan that gives another developer enough context to implement a change.

use_cases.title: Review Implementation Scope
use_cases.description: Break a proposal into concrete steps before estimating effort, dependencies, and testing needs.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an implementation plan for this requirement: [requirement]. Include tasks, affected files, tests, and verification commands.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the requirement is clear and limited in scope.

prompt_templates.title: Plan From a Specification
prompt_templates.prompt: Read [specification path] and create a detailed plan. Identify architecture decisions, exact files, tests, commands, and expected results.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when a written specification already exists.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Repository Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the repository for [feature]. Produce test-first tasks that follow existing patterns and include documentation updates.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when repository conventions must guide the plan.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Complex Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan the migration from [current state] to [target state]. Include dependencies, incremental checkpoints, rollback considerations, tests, and execution handoff.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for changes spanning multiple components or release stages.

output_examples.input: Plan adding account lockout after five failed sign-in attempts.
output: Goal: Add configurable account lockout while preserving existing authentication behavior.
Task 1: Add failing service tests for attempt tracking, lock duration, and successful reset.
Task 2: Implement attempt storage and lock checks, then run the focused test suite.
Task 3: Add integration coverage, update configuration documentation, and verify all authentication tests.

output_examples.input: Plan migrating the notification worker to a new queue provider.
output: Architecture: Introduce a queue adapter so producers remain independent from the provider.
Tasks cover adapter contracts, provider configuration, worker migration, failure handling, and staged rollout.
Each task names affected files, required tests, verification commands, expected results, and a commit checkpoint.

best_practices: Provide the complete specification and relevant repository context.
Review proposed file paths and commands against the current codebase.
Keep each task small enough to test and commit independently.
anti_patterns: Do not request a plan before requirements are stable.
Do not accept placeholder steps without files, tests, or expected outcomes.
Do not execute example commands without reviewing them for the target repository.

faq.question: Does this skill write production code?
faq.answer: No. It creates an implementation plan that another agent or developer can execute.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the specification, repository context, constraints, and acceptance criteria.

faq.question: Does the plan include testing?
faq.answer: Yes. Each task uses test-first steps with expected failure and success results.

faq.question: Where are plans saved?
faq.answer: The skill directs plans to dated Markdown files under the repository documentation plan directory.

faq.question: Can it plan changes across several components?
faq.answer: Yes. It can organize multi-component work into ordered tasks with dependencies and checkpoints.

faq.question: Does it run commands or create commits?
faq.answer: No. It documents commands and commit checkpoints for later execution.
